Send message · long: chat in the app
Video and chat side by side

OK opens the control bar · ≡ (menu) opens "More" · ◀ ▶ switch the channel (live) or jump 10 s (VOD) · ▲ channel switcher (▲ ▼ again switch the list) · channel ± and ⏮ ⏭ switch too · Info shows the statistics · Captions toggles the chat · ⏩ jumps back to live · holding OK repeats nothing.
Profile picture, viewers, uptime, category and title while the control bar is open
Only under the highlighted button (more buttons fit)

Up in the player opens the channel switcher. With "Up/Down switch the channel list" on, every further Up shows the next list and Down the previous one; Down on the first list closes it. Switch off the lists you never use: they are skipped. If all are off, "Followed" stays. Applies to the next time you open the switcher.

In the channel switcher, Up shows the next list (followed, same category, same category in your language, recently watched, top streams, top in your language) and Down the previous one; Left/Right browse the cards. Off: the lists are buttons
With the quality "Audio only" (or the yellow key) the picture is replaced by a black screen with the clock, channel and title, which moves every minute. Off: plain black
Clock, chat and info corner drift slowly by a few pixels (for OLED TVs)

Audio only: pick "Audio only" in the quality menu or press the yellow key; OK returns to the picture, the chat stays usable. Rest screen: a long pause turns the screen dark with clock and channel in changing places; any key continues.

In live streams the bar shows "Replay" right after "Quality": it jumps back a little (into the recording if needed) and returns to live by itself once that part has played. "Live", switching the channel or seeking end it early.

If the picture buffers or stands still for 10 seconds while it should play, the stream is loaded again (live at the live edge, recordings at the same spot), at most three times; then the error shows. Ad breaks do not count.

Up on the control bar selects a timeline from the start of the stream; left/right on it jump back into the recording Twitch makes during the broadcast, with its chat and categories. "Live" returns. Off: only the short live window can be rewound.
More than 30 s behind the live edge (e.g. after a pause): grey LIVE with the delay and a "Live" button in the control bar
Switch to the next followed live channel after 15 s
Only suggest the next channel (OK switches)
When the channel raids another one, a card offers to follow: OK joins, Back stays

Choose where the chat goes under Chat → Layout → "Chat layout": next to the video (nothing is covered), over the video, or transparent. In the player, the "Chat layout" button in the control bar switches between next to the video and over the video with one press; "More" → "Adjust chat" changes layout, width and side live with ◀ ▶.

Separate words or user names with commas, case does not matter. Words get a background, messages of these users (and of the streamer, moderators or VIPs if switched on) a bar on the left and a light background, all in the highlight colour. Mentions of your own name are always marked.

Connects ShrugTV to Home Assistant through your MQTT broker (e.g. the Mosquitto add-on). 1. Enter the broker address, user and password. 2. Switch it on. 3. In Home Assistant the TV appears by itself under Settings → Devices → MQTT, with status, channel, picture, controls and events (raid, stream ended, followed channel live) for automations. Active while ShrugTV is open and 2 minutes after; when the app is closed, start a channel with the ADB deep link shrugtv://stream/<channel>. Without TLS (ssl://) user and password go through the network unencrypted.
Stored separately and not included in backups
How this TV is called in Home Assistant, e.g. Living room; also gives the device id. Empty: the model name.
Play/pause, channel, chat, volume, notices (e.g. doorbell with camera picture). Off: Home Assistant only sees what is playing.
Shows whether ShrugTV is connected to the broker

How this TV appears on the broker. Topics: <topic prefix>/<device id>/state, …/cmd/…, …/event; the device id comes from the device name (lowercase letters, digits, underscores). Every TV should have its own name: if another TV already uses it, this TV adds a short code to its id by itself (shown in the browser settings). When the name or a prefix changes, ShrugTV removes the old entities from Home Assistant itself. Tip: give the TV its own broker user, allowed only on these topics and on the discovery prefix.
Start of every topic, default shrugtv. Letters, digits, _ - and /; names of other systems (zigbee2mqtt, tasmota, homeassistant …) are refused and shrugtv is used
Topic prefix and discovery prefix – usually nothing to change

Only needed for special broker setups. ShrugTV writes only below its own topic prefix and its own discovery entries (shrugtv_<device id>), so other MQTT devices are never touched; several TVs work without changing anything here.
Only change it if Home Assistant was set up with another one (default homeassistant)
How often uptime and VOD position are sent while something plays; changes are sent at once anyway

Choose which entities Home Assistant gets. Switching a group off removes its entities from Home Assistant cleanly, switching it on brings them back. In the browser settings each group shows how many entities it has.
Status, channel, title, category, viewers, uptime
Profile picture of the channel that is playing
Snapshot of the stream, Twitch refreshes it every few minutes
Raid, stream ended, followed channel live, ad break – for automations

Use your phone as remote and keyboard, without an app: 1. Switch it on. 2. Choose "Connect a phone" (or "Phone" in the player\'s More menu) and scan the QR code with a phone in the same Wi-Fi. 3. On the phone: see what is playing, control the TV, read and write the chat with the phone keyboard, search channels and send them to the TV. 4. On a computer: open the address shown with the QR code in the browser and enter the PIN; the tab "Settings" there changes every setting of this app with mouse and keyboard: groups in the sidebar, search with / or Ctrl+K, ☆ pins a setting, every group has its own address for bookmarks, backup to a file (without MQTT and companion, they belong to this TV), light or dark. 5. Tab "Log": what ShrugTV is doing, live; filter by level and source, search, click a line for details, copy or save it for a bug report. Paired devices are remembered and reconnect without a code (list under "Connected devices"). Only in the home network, only while ShrugTV is open.
Shows a QR code and a PIN for the phone
Messages are sent with the Twitch account of this TV
Connected phones and computers can change all settings of this app
Tab "Log": ShrugTV\'s own log, live, with filters, search and export for bug reports. Tokens and passwords are always removed.
Every phone and computer has to scan the QR code or enter the PIN again

On: a phone or computer must be paired once with the QR code or PIN. Off (default): every device in your home network opens the page at the address straight away and may use the remote, the chat with the Twitch account of this TV and, if allowed below, all settings. Never reachable from outside your network.
Phones and computers paired once reconnect by themselves, also after a restart, without a new code
Remembered phones and computers, when they were last used; remove single devices
These phones and computers connect without a code. OK on a device and OK again removes it; it then needs the QR code or PIN again.
No devices remembered yet. Connect one with "Connect a phone".
Press OK again to remove this device

Makes the chat easier to read from the sofa (like the 7TV browser extension): name colours (as chosen, made readable, or all in the accent colour), alternating row backgrounds, a thin line between messages, compact spacing for more messages on the screen, and badges on or off. Changes apply to the next channel you open.
Shows the time at the top right while the control bar of the player is open. Format and date below; the world clocks have no effect yet.

Marks the categories (games) of a recording on the timeline and adds buttons and keys (channel up/down, next/previous) to jump to the next or previous one. Pressing left/right again and again seeks in growing steps.
Shows the chat of a recording (VOD) while it plays, in step with the picture. Read only.
Every second message on a slightly lighter background

When many people send the same text (e.g. \"!100\"), the first line stays and shows \"×12\" instead of twelve lines. Case and spaces do not count; the counter keeps going while the text repeats within the chosen time. Applies from the next chat start.
How a new message comes in: older lines slide up and the new one fades in, only fade in, or a hard cut as before. Applies from the next chat start.
Less space between lines and messages
Off: no badges before the names (moderator, subscriber, 7TV …)

Which emotes the chat shows besides Twitch\'s own: 7TV, BetterTTV and FrankerFaceZ, each on or off (fewer providers = faster start). Zero-width emotes such as hats or rain are drawn over the emote before them instead of next to it. 7TV name colours (gradients), 7TV badges and personal 7TV emotes appear for chatters who use 7TV, as in the 7TV browser extension; they come from 7TV\'s live service. Changes apply to the next channel you open.
Overlay emotes (hats, rain, masks) over the emote before them
Names in the colour gradients that 7TV users chose
Badges of 7TV supporters and staff after the Twitch badges
Emotes that 7TV subscribers may use in every channel
Messages of the streamer with a bar and background
Messages of moderators with a bar and background
Messages of VIPs with a bar and background
For highlighted words, users and roles

Shows the last messages from before you opened the channel, so the chat is not empty at the start. They come from the third-party service recent-messages.robotty.de, which keeps the recent messages of public Twitch channels; switching it on sends the channel name there. Off by default.
